incident_spec.summary: Unpredictable single insert performance in SQL Server due to blocking behavior and excessive indexes.
symptoms: Single record insert takes several minutes.
Blocking session IDs appear in sys.dm_exec_requests but the blocker session is not active.
Wait type observed is LCK_M_S (shared lock).
incident_spec.mechanism: Blocking caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks, exacerbated by excessive indexes.

facts.evidence: The post mentions blocked sessions with session IDs that appear inactive.
The post explicitly mentions LCK_M_S as the wait type.
The post mentions the table has 34 indexes despite being in an OLTP system.

assumptions: The blocking behavior is caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks.
Excessive indexes contribute to the poor insert performance.
unknowns: Exact schema of the table and indexes.
Whether the blocking sessions are caused by application behavior or SQL Server configuration.

feasibility.rationale: The reproduction of blocking behavior and excessive index impact is feasible using synthetic data and controlled experiments.
unmatched_conditions: Exact schema and index definitions are unknown.

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Communication (id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, comm_action NVARCHAR(255), comm_channelid INT, payload NVARCHAR(MAX))
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comm_action ON Communication(comm_action)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comm_channelid ON Communication(comm_channelid)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payload ON Communication(payload)
generation_sql: INSERT INTO Communication (comm_action, comm_channelid, payload) SELECT CONCAT('Action_', n), n % 10, CONCAT('Payload_', n) FROM (SELECT TOP {row_count} ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n FROM sys.objects) AS numbers
